Apple is about to launch a major new smart home offensive. Bloomberg published a report today, revealing that Apple has three brand-new smart home devices that are "nearly ready." The first two are expected to launch in just a few months...

Three brand-new Apple smart home products are nearing completion

According to the report, Apple will launch a brand-new Apple TV set-top box and an updated HomePod mini this autumn. These products will "look similar to the current versions," but internally will feature faster chips to support Apple Intelligence.

For reference, the existing Apple TV 4K uses the A15 Bionic chip. The existing HomePod mini uses the S5 chip, the same processor used in the Apple Watch Series 5.

More excitingly, Apple's long-awaited next-generation smart home hub is also "nearly complete." According to the report, the product is expected to make its debut sometime between "October and early next year."

The product currently has two versions under development. One features a design with "a screen mounted on a hemispherical base," while the other is designed to be "mounted on a wall via a brand-new magnetic attachment system."

Today's report also revisited the device's specifications and features. It is said to feature a 7-inch square display, centered around Apple Intelligence. The device will run a "new operating system" based on tvOS, with the interface described as a "hybrid" of tvOS and watchOS, featuring apps, icons, and widgets.

It will also support FaceTime, home security monitoring, HomeKit integration, and Apple Watch-like customizable watch faces.

However, the most eye-catching feature is expected to be facial recognition:

Finally, Bloomberg noted that Apple has two additional smart home products still in development, to be released later. These include a "smart home hub premium robotic version" with a 9-inch display, and an "advanced indoor security camera."
